title: [Audit] API key inventory
description: One row per API key id seen in range, busiest first: its name, owner, first and last use, volume, client IP spread and indices touched. A re-issued key keeps its name under a new id, so a name can appear more than once. Owner is the creator's email, which Elasticsearch stamps on events from Elasticsearch API keys; Cloud API keys record no owner.
esql: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE attributes.api_key.name IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip), indices = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices) BY api_key = attributes.api_key.name, key_id = attributes.api_key.id, owner = attributes.user.email | EVAL owner = COALESCE(owner, "none recorded") | KEEP api_key, key_id, owner, first_seen, last_seen, events, ips, indices | SORT events DESC | RENAME api_key AS `API key`, key_id AS `Key ID`, owner AS Owner, first_seen AS `First seen`, last_seen AS `Last seen`, events AS Events, ips AS IPs, indices AS Indices
